title: Bias, Fairness, and Societal Impact of Biomedical AI
audience: Clinical learners reflecting on bias and fairness in clinical AI
objectives: Imagine a useful clinical AI system and identify fairness safeguards.
Analyze possible bias vectors in an emergency-room triage algorithm.
Explain risks from regional mismatch, demographic features, subjective inputs, and overreliance.
Reflect on post-deployment fairness monitoring in clinical settings.

sections.name: Ideal Clinical AI System
sections.purpose: Prompt learners to design a clinical AI tool with fairness safeguards.
sections.how_to_use: Describe what the system would do, why it is clinically useful, what data it would use, and how bias would be mitigated.

sections.name: Algorithmic Triage Case Study
sections.purpose: Analyze fairness risks in a trauma-center triage algorithm.
sections.how_to_use: Read the case and write possible bias vectors, deployment considerations, and negative patient-care outcomes.

sections.name: Reflection and Takeaways
sections.purpose: Connect clinical AI fairness to monitoring and safe deployment.
sections.how_to_use: Write why societal impact matters and how fairness would be monitored after deployment.

chatbot_guidance: When asked how to use this notebook, guide the learner through the ideal-system prompt, the triage case, and reflection.
For clinical users, emphasize local population mismatch, trauma-center context, subjective clinical inputs, automation bias, and patient harm.
Help learners identify both data bias and human interpretation bias.
